books.section: America in an Era of Turmoil (1960-1975)

source: original; stimulus table compiled from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Monthly Labor Review, December 1999, Table 1

stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Monthly Labor Review, December 1999, Table 1.
stimulus.text:
Share of adults in paid work (the civilian labor force), by sex (Bureau of Labor Statistics, Monthly Labor Review, December 1999, Table 1):

| Year | Women | Men |
| 1950 | 33.9% | 86.4% |
| 1960 | 37.7% | 83.3% |
| 1970 | 43.3% | 79.7% |
| 1980 | 51.5% | 77.4% |

stem: What does the table show about women and paid work from 1950 to 1980?

options.text: The share of women in paid work fell steadily.
options.misconception: The women's column rises at every step, from 33.9 percent to 51.5 percent.

options.text: The share of women in paid work stayed about the same.
options.misconception: The women's column rises by nearly 18 points, from 33.9 percent to 51.5 percent.

options.text: The share of women in paid work rose steadily, passing half by 1980.
Women took part in paid work at higher rates than men by 1980.
options.misconception: In 1980 the table gives women 51.5 percent and men 77.4 percent, so men were still higher.

rationales.A: The women's column rises at every step, from 33.9 percent to 51.5 percent.
rationales.B: The women's column rises by nearly 18 points, from 33.9 percent to 51.5 percent.
rationales.C: The women's column rises at every step, from 33.9 percent in 1950 to 51.5 percent in 1980.
rationales.D: In 1980 the table gives women 51.5 percent and men 77.4 percent, so men were still higher.
rationales.general:
1. Read the women's column only: 33.9, 37.7, 43.3, 51.5 percent.
2. Each number is larger than the one before it, and the last one passes 50 percent.
3. The men's column answers a different question, so it cannot change what the women's column shows.
Remember: Read one column at a time and compare each number with the one before it.
